Seattle movers cost: what a crew charges and why

A 2-bedroom home moved 10 road miles costs $720–$1,800, with a crew of 3 at $150–$225 an hour, off peak, with no stairs or extras. Seattle movers cost more than that on most real moves: steep streets, walk-ups, scarce curb space and bridge traffic all add billed hours. Washington's tariff then sets the lowest and highest rate a licensed mover may charge.

What Seattle movers cost by the hour

Inside the Seattle area, a move of 55 miles or less is billed by the hour: the number of workers, the time it takes to load, drive and unload, and the mover's hourly rate. Each mover adds $50–$75 an hour. A studio or 1-bedroom usually takes 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour, a 3-bedroom house 4 movers at $200–$300 an hour, and a home of 4 or more bedrooms 5 movers at $250–$375 an hour. That is what Seattle movers cost before the clock starts.

In total, a typical local move of a 1-bedroom home costs $380–$960 and a 3-bedroom home $1,150–$2,850, at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras. These are national figures from the rate table behind the calculator, not Seattle quotes. Wages are part of the gap: the pay panel below shows moving crews in the Seattle metro earn more an hour than the national typical, and Seattle movers cost what they do partly because the people carrying your sofa are paid more.

Washington's tariff: a floor and a ceiling on Seattle movers cost

Washington regulates movers more closely than most states. The Utilities and Transportation Commission (UTC) sets the minimum and maximum prices a licensed, in-state mover may charge for a household move, in a document called Tariff 15-C. Companies choose their rates inside that range, which is why Seattle movers cost different amounts from one permitted company to the next, but none may charge less than the minimum or more than the maximum.

For you, that means Seattle movers cost within a known band, as long as you hire a mover with a UTC permit. Every company moving household goods within Washington needs one, and the UTC warns that some unlicensed movers hold goods until a large payment is made or raise estimates illegally. Look up a mover's permit before you book, because the commission can do very little for you if you hire a company without one.

The 55-mile line: Tacoma, Everett and Olympia

The UTC's Consumer Guide to Moving in Washington State splits moves by distance, and the split decides how Seattle movers cost is worked out. A move of 55 miles or less is priced by the hour. A move of 56 miles or more is priced by the weight of your goods and the distance hauled: the mover weighs the empty truck, then weighs it again once it's loaded. If you ask, the mover tells you the weight and the charges, and you can watch the official weighing.

From Seattle, that line sorts the common routes neatly. Bellevue, Redmond, Everett and Tacoma are well inside it, so those moves are hourly and the drive is billed as crew time. Olympia, about 60 miles south, sits just past it, and Bellingham farther still, so those moves are priced by weight and miles. If your other address is near the line, ask each mover which way it will price the job, because Seattle movers cost very different amounts under the two methods.

Hills, walk-ups and the curb

Seattle's hills are part of the bill. Queen Anne, Capitol Hill, Magnolia and parts of West Seattle have steep blocks where a truck can't park level, and many older apartment buildings are walk-ups with narrow stairs. Newer townhouses often stack their rooms over three or four floors, so every bedroom's furniture goes up a staircase. The calculator asks about stairs and adds crew time for them, and stairs are where Seattle movers cost climbs fastest.

The curb is the other half. On a busy street, a truck with nowhere to park leaves the crew carrying every load from down the block, and that walk is billed. The local rules below explain how to reserve curb space for the moving truck through the Seattle Department of Transportation, and the permit a truck needs to use it. In an apartment building, book the freight elevator and loading area with the manager as well. A legal space right outside the door is one of the cheapest ways to keep Seattle movers cost down on the day.

Rain, bridges and ferries

From October through April, Seattle's rainy season changes how a crew works. Movers wrap furniture more carefully, lay floor runners in both homes and carry more slowly on wet stairs and ramps, and on an hourly bill that care takes time. The calculator prices those months as off peak, so Seattle movers cost less in winter on rate even though the crew works a little slower in the rain.

Water shapes the drive as well. A move to the Eastside crosses Lake Washington on Interstate 90 or State Route 520, and SR 520 is a toll bridge, so ask whether the toll is billed to you. A move to Bainbridge Island or Vashon Island means a Washington State Ferries crossing, where large vehicles pay a fare by length and the crew waits for the boat on the clock. Seattle movers cost more for an island move than the road miles alone suggest.

Estimates, the 25% cap and paying at delivery

Washington movers must give you a free written estimate before the move, and it should describe every charge clearly. A binding estimate guarantees the price for the items and services it lists. With a non-binding estimate, the final bill can be higher, but under UTC rules no more than 25% above the estimate or any supplemental estimate. If anything changes, the mover must give you a supplemental estimate to sign before it does the extra work, so Seattle movers cost what you have agreed in writing.

An estimate is only as accurate as what you show the mover, so show it everything: the attic, the garage, the shed, the closets and what's stored under the beds. If the final charges on a non-binding estimate run above it, the UTC guide says paying 110% of the estimate gets your goods unloaded, and the mover must give you 30 days to pay any balance. Read the bill of lading, your contract with the mover, before you sign it, and keep a copy until everything is unpacked. That paperwork is what pins Seattle movers cost to the price you agreed.

Choosing damage cover on a Washington move

The UTC guide gives three levels of mover liability, and the level you pick changes what Seattle movers cost on the bill:

  • Option 1, basic value protection. It costs nothing extra but pays only a set amount per pound for a lost or damaged item, whatever the item is worth.
  • Option 2, replacement cost with a deductible. This is the default if you don't choose an option on the bill of lading. It costs extra, priced on the declared value of your goods.
  • Option 3, replacement cost with no deductible. This is the fullest cover, and it costs the most.

Read the exclusions before you rely on any of them. The guide says the mover isn't responsible for furniture made of pressed board or particle board, for breakage in boxes you packed unless you can prove the mover was negligent, or for jewelry, cash and valuable papers. Options 2 and 3 don't apply to antiques, fine art and similar irreplaceable items. Flat-pack furniture can therefore carry risk that no option on Seattle movers cost covers, so take it apart and pad it well.

If something does break, you have nine months from delivery to file a written claim with the mover, and you should keep the damaged item for it to inspect. Check your own home insurance as well, because the UTC points out that mover liability is not the same thing as insurance.

A Capitol Hill walk-up to a Ballard townhouse

Say you're moving a 1-bedroom apartment on the third floor of a Capitol Hill walk-up to a three-story townhouse in Ballard, about 5 road miles away. A typical local 1-bedroom move costs $380–$960, with 2 movers at $100–$150 an hour, off peak, with no stairs or extras. Here, the stairs at both ends drive most of what Seattle movers cost for the job:

  • three flights down at the old address and two flights up at the new one add carrying time;
  • without reserved curb space, the crew may carry every load from down the block;
  • a Saturday in August is peak season, when crews book up first;
  • a packing service for 1 bedroom adds $300–$650.

Move the same apartment on a weekday in March, reserve the curb at both ends and pack it yourself, and much of that extra time disappears. Enter both ZIP codes, your stairs and your date in the calculator above to see what Seattle movers cost for this move or yours. It's free and needs no email to see the price.

Getting a firm Seattle movers cost

  1. Get your range from the calculator above. It's free, takes about a minute and needs no email to see the price.
  2. Look up each mover's UTC permit before you book.
  3. Ask two or three permitted movers for a written estimate, binding if they offer one, for the same inventory and date.
  4. Ask how each prices travel time, stairs, the curb and any toll or ferry fare.
  5. Choose a liability option on the bill of lading, rather than taking the default by accident.

Hold each written estimate against the calculator's range and the UTC's tariff band, and ask about anything far outside them. That way, what Seattle movers cost on paper is what you pay on moving day.

Reserving Seattle curb space for the moving truck

A legal space by your door keeps Seattle movers cost down, because a long carry is billed. Here are the city's rules for reserving curb space and permitting the moving truck, each with its source.

Reserve a Temporary No Parking Zone for the moving van

Temporary No Parking Zones provide curb space for moving vans, and you apply through the Seattle Services Portal. For a non-paid space, the No-Parking easels with the printed public notice should be placed 72 hours in advance, though Parking Enforcement needs only 24 hours' notice to enforce the zone.

Source: Seattle Department of Transportation, checked 28 October 2026

Get a Restricted Area Truck Permit for the moving truck

A moving truck needs a Restricted Area Truck Permit to use a Temporary No Parking Zone. Apply online, or at the Customer Service kiosk on the 4th floor of the Seattle Municipal Tower.

Source: Seattle Department of Transportation, checked 28 October 2026

If Seattle movers cost more than you planned, compare the same move three ways: a rental truck you drive up the hills yourself, a container a company hauls, and a full crew with its own truck.

For it

  • The renter sets the schedule and the pace, and decides whether to bring in help. (HireAHelper)
  • U-Haul's one-way rate is a flat rate that includes a set number of rental days and a mileage allowance for the route. (HireAHelper)
  • Most rental companies let a truck be picked up in one city and returned in another. (HireAHelper)

Against it

  • No storage time comes with a truck: loading, the drive and unloading all run on one timeline. (HireAHelper)
  • Finding space to park a large truck can be hard, especially in cities. (HireAHelper)
  • The renter drives the truck, in city traffic and on the highway. (HireAHelper)

Seattle moving timeline, from estimates to the last walk-through

Starting early keeps Seattle movers cost down, from getting three estimates to checking your building's rules. Enter your moving date to see each task, week by week, up to the final walk-through.

0 of 14 done

8 weeks before

  • Look at how each one handled problems, not only at the star rating.

  • Give each one the same details, so the prices compare like for like.

6 weeks before

  • Moving hours, elevators, loading docks and gates. If one wants the company's certificate of insurance, ask the company to send it ahead.

4 weeks before

  • Get a few extra: the last rooms to pack often need more than planned.

2 weeks before

  • Get a name and a direct number, not only the main office line.

  • Plan how those will travel, or give them away before moving day.

1 week before

  • Keys, gate or door codes, and someone there to let them in.

The day before

  • Tape a sign on it, or gather it in one room, so it isn't loaded by mistake.

Moving day

  • Photograph each page if no copy is handed to you.

  • Match the names on the boxes, so each one lands in the right room.

  • Look high and low: top shelves, under sinks, the attic and the garage.

After the move

  • Ask your state's motor vehicle office how long you have to do it.

  • Say what went well and what didn't; it helps the next person choosing.

  • Insurers, subscriptions, clients, payroll: anyone who sends you mail or money.

Questions

Seattle movers cost: what a crew charges and why FAQ

Can't find your answer? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com.

What hidden fees show up on a short Seattle move?

Ask about a minimum number of hours, travel time to your door, stairs, a long carry from the truck, packing materials, and any bridge toll or ferry fare. On a small job, those extras can make Seattle movers cost far more than the hourly rate suggests. Get every charge listed in the written estimate, which Washington movers must give you for free.

How much should you tip a Seattle moving crew?

Tipping is up to you, and it sits outside what Seattle movers cost on the bill. Moving guides suggest $10.00–$20.00 per mover for a job of up to 4 hours, and $20.00–$65.00 per mover for each full working day. Tip toward the top after a walk-up, a long carry or a day of rain.

What does a 2,000-square-foot Seattle house cost to move?

Movers price what you own, not floor area, but as a rough rule of thumb 2,000 square feet is often a 3-bedroom house. A typical local 3-bedroom move costs $1,150–$2,850 at 10 road miles, off peak, with no stairs or extras, with 4 movers at $200–$300 an hour. Seattle movers cost more than that for a house with stairs, a steep driveway or a long carry.

Do Seattle movers cost less in winter?

Usually, yes. The calculator prices any date from October through April as off peak, and crews have more open dates then. Rain slows the work a little, so Seattle movers cost less in winter mainly through lower rates and easier booking, not faster crews. A mid-month weekday is the cheapest slot in any season.
